question.text: In the 20th century, this Southern Hemisphere country built a nearly 3500-mile fence to keep dingos, a type of wild dog that lives in this country's outback, out of its more populated southeast.
question.clue: This country's longest serving prime minister was Robert Menzies, who founded its Liberal Party and famously called the middle class, "The Forgotten People".

swap.text: The "history wars" began after the Bringing Them Home report was released on these people. This term refers to Australian Aborigines taken from their families as children by the Australian government.
swap.clue: An official 2007 apology to these people and their descendants was made by then-Prime Minister Kevin Rudd.

question.leadin: This colony was founded by the First Fleet on January 26, 1788, and its first governor was Arthur Phillip.
question.text: Name this colony which originated around Port Jackson. Lachlan Macquarie was the final governor of this territory.
question.clue: George Johnston and John Macarthur led forces during an 1808 event in this colony.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the failure of the Gallipoli Campaign.
swap.text: The date of the Gallipoli landing is a day of remembrance for this expeditionary force, which was composed of soldiers from two British commonwealths.
swap.answerHtml: ANZAC [or the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps]
swap.clue: Their most notable action is remembered in the song titled "And the Band Played" a certain nationalist folk tune, was supported by the French from Kum Kale, and was advocated by Winston Churchill.

question.leadin: Australia has struggled with the civil rights of these people.
question.text: These indigenous Australians were frequently massacred at the beginning of British colonization of Australia.
question.clue: Many of these people were taken from their families and integrated into white culture, becoming the Stolen Generation.

swap.leadin: Malcolm Fraser came to power after a 1975 constitutional crisis in Australia.
swap.text: Fraser succeeded Gough (goff) Whitlam, the leader of this political party, which shares its name, but not its American-style spelling, with one of the two main parties in the U.K.
swap.clue: This political party passed important social reforms under leaders like Bob Hawke and Gough Whitlam.

question.leadin: As Treasurer of Australia, this man oversaw the creation of the Australian Dollar and later ended the pegging of the currency to the British pound.
question.text: Name this Prime Minister who more famously went missing while swimming at Cheviot Beach in 1967. Ironically, a swimming pool in Melbourne was named in his honor.
question.clue: This prime minister declared that he was "all the way with LBJ" in showing his country's support for the Vietnam War.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a World War I battle.
swap.text: This military group, composed of soldiers from two nations, landed at Gallipoli at its namesake cove, but was disbanded after the campaign's failure.
swap.answer: Australian and New Zealand Army Corps
swap.clue: Alexander Godley collaborated with William Birdwood to oversee its operations, which didn't formally cease until another branch of it disbanded after Villers-Bretonneux.

question.text: The band Midnight Oil wore jackets with "SORRY" on the back to draw attention to the Stolen Generations during the 2000 Summer Olympics in this Australian city. This is the most populous city in Australia.
question.clue: This city is the largest to be served by the Snowy Mountains Hydroelectric Scheme, whose construction caused its country to ease pro-white immigration policies.

swap.text: Discontent within the Australian mining community and anger at British rule led to the proto-democratic demands of the Forest Creek Monster Meeting, which culminated in this 1854 rebellion at Ballarat, forcing the British to institute reforms.
swap.clue: This conflict turned violent with the murder of James Scobie, which prompted the Peter Lalor-led "diggers" to form the Ballarat Reform League.

question.text: This bushranger belonged to the Greta mob and a later "gang" named after him. While under siege by the police at Glenrowan, this man wore an iron bulletproof suit.
question.clue: This man sent a lewd note wrapped around calves' testicles to Jeremiah McCormack's wife.

swap.text: In 2017, Australian Aboriginals and Torres Strait Islanders held a convention at this rock formation in central Australia that is sacred to local tribes.
swap.clue: A major event in the Aboriginal Rights Movement was the 1985 ceremony that returned ownership of this monolith to the Anangu. A 99-year lease on this enormous monolith has kept the Anangu from forbidding people to climb it.

question.leadin: A leader of this party named Johannes Strydom was nicknamed "Lion of the North."
question.text: Identify this party, which first won a majority in parliament in a 1948 election under Daniel Francois Malan's leadership. Its government implemented the Group Areas Act and the Land Acts.
question.clue: This defunct right-wing party first led by J. B. M. Hertzog, who formed a government after defeating the United Party led by Jan Smuts in 1924.

swap.leadin: Robert Hughes's history The Fatal Shore describes the many lesbians who were imprisoned at this island's Cascades Female Factory in the 1840s.
swap.text: Name this island where the explorer John Franklin's wife Jane founded apple orchards and a Royal Society. The novel English Passengers fictionalizes Manx settlers of this island's colony of Van Diemen's Land.
swap.answerHtml: Tasmania [or lutruwita; accept Royal Society of Tasmania; reject “Australia”] (Matthew Kneale wrote English Passengers.)
swap.clue: In 1996, Martin Bryant killed 35 people on this island.

question.text: Menzies built credit among the middle class by calling them by this name, which titles a notable 1942 speech he made emphasizing his connections to ordinary people.

swap.text: On February 19, 1942, this capital city of the Northern Territory experienced the only major assault on Australian soil during World War II when it was bombed by the Japanese.
swap.clue: This city was originally named after Lord Palmerston.

question.text: Later, New Zealand and Australia laid out their post-WWII military and political goals in the Canberra Pact, signed by this Australian prime minister. Frank Forde finished this prime minister's term after his death in office.
question.clue: This prime minister of Australia during World War Two, a member of the Labour Party, defended the policy by declaring the country "the home of the British race" in a 1942 speech.

swap.leadin: An incredibly strong worker known as Crooked Mick appears in folktales about a mythical one of these places called the Speewah.
swap.text: Name these places, such as Anna Creek and Victoria Downs. Subsidiaries of these places, prefixed with the word "out-," also name remote communities of Aboriginal Australians.
swap.answerHtml: stations [accept cattle stations; accept sheep stations; accept outstations; prompt on cattle ranches]

question.leadin: Matthew Brady, not to be confused with the American photographer, was known as a "gentleman" one of these people and was an enemy of Governor George Arthur. FTPE.
question.text: Identify this group of outlaws that included Ned Kelly.
question.clue: "Bolters" like John "Black" Caesar made up the first generation of this profession, whose later practitioners included Mary Ann Bugg and her lover, Captain Thunderbolt.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of convict-era Australia.
swap.text: The Australian-born children of emancipated convicts were known by this term, contrasted with "sterling" or English-born settlers.
swap.clue: Edible examples of these items include Mongolian tea bricks, and, in Rome, salt.
